validated_results.title: A U-shaped association between blood selenium levels and prostate cancer: findings of a case-control study among Nigerian men.
validated_results.reason: This hospital-based matched case-control study assessed the association between whole blood selenium concentrations and incident prostate cancer risk in Nigerian men.

extraction.population: Male patients attending urology and general outpatient clinics at Nnamdi Azikiwe University Teaching Hospital, Nnewi, Nigeria

sample_size.excerpt: A total of 285 participants: PCa ( n = 90), BPH patients ( n = 97) and Control participants ( n = 98) were included in the study.
sample_size.location: Methods, Study population, paragraph 1; total_n derived from reported group counts 90 + 98 = 188

cases.excerpt: We studied the associations between selenium exposure and prostate diseases such as prostate cancer (PCa) and benign prostatic hyperplasia (BPH), and estimated the optimal range of selenium concentrations that may be needed to prevent these diseases among Nigerian men. Blood and urine samples from men with histologically diagnosed PCa ( n = 90), BPH ( n = 97), and controls ( n = 98) were analyzed for trace elements, including selenium.
